key_insight: Introducing RBench, a standardized robotics-focused benchmark and evaluation suite that reframes video generation for the embodied world—enabling consistent assessment of how well models capture perception, reasoning, and action in real robot interactions.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a standardized benchmark and evaluation protocol for synthesizing high-quality, realistic robot interaction videos, which has hampered fair comparison and progress in embodied video generation.
method: Curate a diverse robotics video dataset covering real-world interactions, multiple tasks, and varied sensors/angles (RBench).
Define evaluation protocols and specialized metrics that quantify perception fidelity, action/causal consistency, and physical plausibility.
Provide baseline model evaluations and an open framework for reproducible comparisons and future method development.
impact: RBench enables researchers and practitioners to reliably compare video generation models for robotics, accelerating progress in data synthesis, sim-to-real transfer, and downstream embodied AI tasks by providing standard data, metrics, and baselines.
visual_elements: Dataset overview grid: thumbnails of diverse robot interaction clips with metadata (task, sensors, viewpoints).
Pipeline diagram: data → model generation → multi-metric evaluation (perception, action consistency, realism).
Radar/bar charts: side-by-side model comparisons across the proposed metrics (perception accuracy, causal/action consistency, realism).
Real vs. generated frame pairs: qualitative examples highlighting common failure modes (misplaced object, incorrect action timing).
paper_title: Rethinking Video Generation Model for the Embodied World
paper_authors: Yufan Deng, Zilin Pan, Hongyu Zhang, Xiaojie Li, Ruoqing Hu
